key_insight: LLMSurgeon shows that you can infer the domain makeup of an LLM’s hidden pretraining data by analyzing only its generated text. This turns the model’s outputs into a practical signal for auditing its “digital DNA.”
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of transparency around LLM pretraining data mixtures, which makes it difficult to audit provenance, detect risky data composition, or understand how specific domain exposure shapes model behavior and failure modes.
method: Formulate Data Mixture Surgery (DMS): estimate the domain-level distribution of a target LLM’s pretraining corpus from generated text alone.
Use a predefined taxonomy of domains to map model outputs back to likely training-data mixture proportions.
Propose LLMSurgeon as the auditing framework for diagnosing and comparing pretraining data composition across models.
impact: For practitioners, this provides a new post-hoc auditing tool for understanding what an LLM was likely trained on, even when training data is undisclosed. It can support model accountability, safer deployment decisions, and better analysis of how data mix influences strengths and weaknesses.

paper_title: LLMSurgeon: Diagnosing Data Mixture of Large Language Models
paper_authors: Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Xiaohan Zhao, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Liu
